lit.\u0027¿Cuántos e⁻ π tiene el anión ciclo: "How many π electrons does the cyclopentadienyl anion have?"
lit.\u0027¿Por qué el pirrol no es básico mi: "Why is pyrrole not basic while pyridine is?"
lit.\u0027\u003cdiv class=\"calc-step\"\u003:
"
3 · Comparison with the open polyene
"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon \u003cb\u003e4 e⁻:
"

With 4 π electrons (cyclobutadiene) or 8 π electrons (planar COT) the last two electrons occupy two degenerate nonbonding MOs: open shell, unpaired and very reactive. The molecule escapes antiaromaticity by distorting: cyclobutadiene becomes rectangular and COT folds into a tub shape (nonaromatic).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eanión:
"

The cyclopentadienyl anion (6 e⁻), the tropylium cation (6 e⁻), the cyclopropenyl cation (2 e⁻) and the COT dianion (10 e⁻) satisfy 4n + 2. They explain why cyclopentadiene has a pKa of ≈ 16 (very acidic for a hydrocarbon) and why tropylium bromide is a stable salt.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el \u003cb\u003ebe:
"

In benzene the six p orbitals overlap in two clouds (toroids) above and below the plane: the π electrons do not belong to three double bonds, but to the whole ring. All six C–C bonds are equal (1.39 Å). Switch between Kekulé (localized) and delocalized in “Lab” and see how the classical model is only one of the resonance forms.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el \u003cb\u003epi:
"

In pyrrole and furan a lone pair of the heteroatom is in a p orbital and contributes 2 electrons to the sextet: 4 + 2 = 6. In pyridine, the N pair is in the plane (sp²) and does not count: the 6 electrons come from the three C=C and N keeps its basicity. That is why pyrrole is not basic and pyridine is.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos n orbitales p de:
"

The n p orbitals of a ring form n molecular orbitals with energies Ek = α + 2β cos(2πk/n). The Frost circle brings them together: a polygon with one vertex at the bottom inscribed in a circle of radius 2|β|. For benzene: one lowest-energy MO, two degenerate ones, two degenerate ones and one of highest energy. The 6 electrons exactly fill the three bonding MOs: closed shell. The blue and red lobes are the phases of the selected MO.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn compuesto es \u003:
"

A compound is aromatic if it is cyclic, planar, with a p orbital on every ring atom (complete conjugation) and has 4n + 2 π electrons (2, 6, 10, 14…). If it meets the rest but has 4n π electrons (4, 8, 12…) it is antiaromatic (destabilized); if it fails any of the structural criteria it is nonaromatic.

"
lit.\u0027«Compuesto» y «Orbital π (de menor: 'compound and π orbital (from lowest to highest energy); the Kekulé / delocalised switch changes the model.'
lit.\u002710 e⁻ π: el anillo se aplana y es: "10 π electrons: the ring flattens and is aromatic (4n + 2 with n = 2). It is obtained with metallic K."
lit.\u00272 e⁻ π (n = 0): el anillo aromátic: "2 π electrons (n = 0): the smallest aromatic ring; it is prepared as a stable salt."
lit.\u00274 de los dos C=C + 2 del par libre: "4 from the two C=C + 2 from the carbanion lone pair = 6: aromatic."
lit.\u00274 e⁻ π: antiaromático, muy inestab: "4 π electrons: antiaromatic, very unstable (not known as a stable species)."
lit.\u00274n electrones π: antiaromático. Se: "4n π electrons: antiaromatic. It distorts to a rectangle (1.34 and 1.57 Å) and is so unstable that it can only be isolated at very low temperature."
lit.\u00276 e⁻ π en 7 C: aromático. Es tan e: "6 π electrons over 7 C: aromatic. It is so stable that it exists as a salt (tropylium bromide)."
lit.\u00276 e⁻ π en un anillo plano de 5 C:: "6 π electrons in a planar 5-carbon ring: aromatic. It explains the acidity of cyclopentadiene (pKa ≈ 16) and ferrocene."
lit.\u0027Cada vértice es un OM π; la altura: "Each vertex is a π MO; the height indicates its energy (down = bonding). Arrows: electrons. The chosen MO is highlighted."
lit.\u0027Cíclica, plana, totalmente conjuga: "Cyclic, planar, fully conjugated and with 4n + 2 π electrons"
lit.\u0027Como el benceno: 6 e⁻ π. El par li: "Like benzene: 6 π electrons. The lone pair of N is in the plane (sp² orbital), outside the π system: pyridine is basic (pKa of the pyridinium ion ≈ 5.2)."
lit.\u0027compara el modelo clásico con la n: "compares the classical model with the π cloud."
lit.\u0027Compara pirrol y piridina: sólo en: 'Compare pyrrole and pyridine: only in pyrrole is the N lone pair part of the π system.'
lit.\u0027Compara un compuesto con 4n + 2 el: 'Compare a compound with 4n + 2 π electrons and one with 4n on the Frost circle.'
lit.\u0027Con \u003cb\u003e4n e⁻ π\u003c/b\u: "With 4n π electrons and planar: antiaromatic (open shell); the molecule distorts to escape."
lit.\u0027Con 4n e⁻ π hay dos electrones des: "With 4n π electrons there are two unpaired electrons in degenerate nonbonding MOs."
lit.\u0027Con 4n electrones π quedan electro: "With 4n π electrons there are unpaired electrons"
lit.\u0027Con 8 e⁻ π un COT plano sería anti: "With 8 π electrons a planar COT would be antiaromatic; it distorts and there is no complete cyclic conjugation."
lit.\u0027E(anillo) − E(polieno abierto con: "E(ring) − E(open polyene with the same atoms and electrons). Positive: aromatic; negative: antiaromatic. (Planar COT has an open shell and folds.)"
lit.\u0027El carbono sp³ (CH₂) interrumpe la: "The sp³ carbon (CH₂) interrupts the conjugation: it is not a fully conjugated cyclic system, so it is not aromatic."
lit.\u0027el control elige un OM entre los n: "the control chooses one MO among the n possible."
lit.\u0027El heteroátomo aporta 0 o 2 electr: "The heteroatom contributes 0 or 2 electrons to the π system"
lit.\u0027El heteroátomo aporta 2 e⁻ si su p: "The heteroatom contributes 2 electrons if its pair is in a p orbital (pyrrole, furan) and 0 if it is in the plane (pyridine)."
lit.\u0027El par libre del N (en un orbital: "The lone pair of N (in a p orbital) contributes 2 electrons to the π system: 4 from the two C=C + 2 = 6. That is why the N of pyrrole is not basic."
lit.\u0027El tropilio tiene 6 e⁻ π en un ani: "Tropylium has 6 π electrons in a planar, fully conjugated ring."
lit.\u0027Elige un compuesto en «Lab» o sigu: "Choose a compound in “Lab” or follow the lesson. The blue/red lobes are the phases of the chosen π orbital; the purple toroids, the delocalized π cloud."
lit.\u0027En el círculo de Frost del benceno: "In the Frost circle of benzene, how many bonding π MOs are there?"
lit.\u0027En el pirrol el par del N forma pa: "In pyrrole the N pair is part of the π sextet; in pyridine it is in the plane"
lit.\u0027Es plano y cíclico con 4 e⁻ π (4n): "It is planar and cyclic with 4 π electrons (4n)"
lit.\u0027Hay un OM de menor energía y dos d: "There is one lowest-energy MO and two degenerate ones, all bonding; the 6 electrons fill them."
lit.\u0027La desprotonación del CH₂ genera e: "Deprotonation of the CH₂ generates the cyclopentadienyl anion, which is aromatic and highly stabilized."
lit.\u0027Los n orbitales p dan n OM: energí: "The n p orbitals give n MOs: energies α + 2β·cos(2πk/n)"
lit.\u0027Los seis enlaces C–C miden 1,39 Å: "All six C–C bonds measure 1.39 Å (neither single nor double). Resonance energy ≈ 150 kJ/mol: it does not hydrogenate or add like an alkene."
lit.\u0027Protonar el N del pirrol destruirí: "Protonating the N of pyrrole would destroy the aromatic sextet; the pyridine pair (sp²) does not participate."
lit.\u0027Recorre los orbitales π de menor a: 'Step through the π orbitals from lowest to highest energy: the number of nodes increases.'
lit.\u0027Se pliega en forma de bote para ev: "It folds into a tub shape to avoid antiaromaticity"
lit.\u0027Seis electrones π deslocalizados s: "Six π electrons delocalized over the whole ring"
lit.\u0027Su base conjugada es aromática (6: "Its conjugate base is aromatic (6 π electrons)"
lit.\u0027Tendría 8 e⁻ π: si fuera plano ser: "It would have 8 π electrons: if planar it would be antiaromatic. It folds into a tub shape and behaves like four isolated double bonds."
lit.\u0027Un anillo con carga también puede: "A charged ring can also be aromatic"
lit.\u0027Un par del O aporta 2 e⁻ al sistem: "One lone pair of O contributes 2 electrons to the π system (the other pair stays in the plane): 6 π electrons, moderately aromatic."
